old: It began as the name for a straight, hollow plant stem used to check whether things measured up.
Its Greek ancestor meant 'measuring rod' before it ever meant 'rule' or 'standard.'
It shares a root with cane, cannon, canyon, and canal — all cousins sprung from the same reed.
clues: This noun for a recognized standard began as an ancient word for a reed, because a straight reed once served as a measuring rod.
Today it often names the official body of works accepted as authentic, such as a religion's approved scriptures or the stories that truly count in a franchise, unlike fan fiction.
Fans argue over whether a surprise plot twist belongs in it. It shares a reed-and-measuring-rod family with cane, canal, canyon, and its sound-alike, the big gun cannon.
